patients.summary: Administrative assistant who joined the practice healthy in 2019. Heavy periods from a submucosal fibroid (resected 2022) led to iron deficiency anemia and then restless legs; pulmonary arterial hypertension was diagnosed by an outside pulmonology group in 2024 and treated with tadalafil. Last seen January 2026 for a wellness visit with ongoing fatigue.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32-year-old woman establishing care. Transferring from another primary care office for easier access; she has had no ongoing problems there.

HISTORY: Generally well. No chronic illnesses. No hospitalizations. Takes no prescription or OTC medicines regularly.
OB/GYN: G1P1, one uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Menses monthly and manageable, about 5 days. Last Pap at prior office, normal per patient; records requested.
Surgical: none apart from the delivery.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: mother has fibroids and restless legs. A maternal aunt has pulmonary arterial hypertension. No other heart, lung or blood disorders she knows of.
Social: administrative assistant, desk work. Never smoked. Does not drink. No drug use.

ROS: negative across systems; no fatigue, dyspnea, bleeding problems.

EXAM: Pleasant, well appearing. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities warm, no swelling. Skin clear. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix appears healthy, uterus normal size and nontender, no adnexal fullness. Pap with HPV obtained.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Adult preventive care. Tdap given today (last tetanus unknown). CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees. PHQ-2 negative.
2. Cervical screening: co-test sent; if negative, next in 5 years.
3. Family history noted; nothing to act on now.
Follow up yearly or as needed. She has the portal and knows she can text.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tamika, your blood count, chemistry panel, thyroid and cholesterol all look healthy. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. The Pap result usually takes a few more days; I'll message you when it posts.

PCP review: nothing outstanding. Consistent with her history.

documents.title: Office Visit: Heavy Menses
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since about July her periods have gotten longer and heavier. Now running well over a week, with big clots, and cramping bad enough that she has left work early twice. Using pads and tampons together on the heaviest days. Cycle still monthly. Not pregnant per her; not currently trying. No bleeding between periods or after intercourse. Mother had fibroids.
O: Looks well. Vitals per flowsheet. Abdomen soft, nontender, no palpable mass.
A: Heavy menstrual bleeding, likely structural given family history.
P: Gynecology referral placed for evaluation and pelvic imaging. She has an opening there in mid-January and would rather have blood drawn once, so the gyn office will check her counts at that visit. Call if she feels faint or soaks a pad an hour.

reports.text: Transvaginal technique. Uterus enlarged, anteverted. A 3 cm well-circumscribed intracavitary mass arises on a stalk from the anterior uterine wall. The endometrium is thickened and heterogeneous around it. Ovaries normal in size and appearance bilaterally. No adnexal mass. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: 3 cm pedunculated submucosal (intracavitary) fibroid from the anterior wall; thickened, heterogeneous endometrium.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE — CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/17/2022
Referring: primary care

Reason: worsening menstrual bleeding.

Ms. Kenney is a 35-year-old G1P1 seen at her PCP's request. Over roughly half a year her flow has become heavier and longer; she now bleeds 10 to 12 days each cycle and passes large clots. Cramps are severe; she says they feel like contractions did in labor.

PMH: none. PSH: SVD x1. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH: mother with fibroids. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Abdomen soft without tenderness. Speculum and bimanual: uterus enlarged, smooth in contour and nontender. A firm, irregular mass is felt at the cervix.

In-office studies: CBC hemoglobin 10.2, hematocrit 30.5, MCV 82, platelets 250. Transvaginal US with a 3 cm intracavitary mass on a stalk off the anterior wall and a thick, heterogeneous lining.

Impression: submucosal leiomyoma, pedunculated, likely prolapsing toward the cervix; menorrhagia; mild anemia.

Plan: discussed options. She would like it removed. Hysteroscopic resection to be scheduled after pre-op; our surgical coordinator will call her. Anemia results forwarded to PCP.

— Gynecology attending

[PCP note on receipt 1/26: read. Fibroid on list. She plans surgery in spring.]

documents.title: Office Visit: Fatigue, Exertional Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: worn out, winded.

HPI: 35F seen about three months after gynecology found a submucosal fibroid. For about three months she has been tired all the time and gets short of breath on exertion, worst on the stairs at work. Periods still heavy and long while she waits for her resection. New since winter: she craves ice and chews it constantly, and admits she sometimes eats little bits of paper, which embarrasses her. No chest pain, palpitations, black stools or blood in the urine. No meds.

Hgb at gyn in January was 10.2.

Exam: tired-appearing. Skin and conjunctivae pale. Spoon-shaped nails on both hands. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No leg swelling. Vitals per flowsheet.

Assessment: fatigue and exertional dyspnea with pica and koilonychia in the setting of menorrhagia from a fibroid. Strongly suspect iron deficiency.

Plan: CBC and iron studies now, I'll call this afternoon. Expect oral iron. Surgery date with gyn pending, she will let us know.

documents.title: Lab results: iron deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with today's results. Hgb 9.2, MCV 70. Iron 30, TIBC 600, ferritin 8 — classic iron deficiency, from the fibroid bleeding. Starting ferrous sulfate 325 mg once daily; take it with orange juice, not with coffee or tea; stools will darken, constipation possible. The ice and paper cravings should fade as iron comes back up. Sent to her pharmacy. Recheck counts after the surgery. She verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Had my surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just wanted you to know I had the hysteroscopy on the 20th and they took the fibroid out. They said it went fine and I went home the same day. Should I keep taking the iron?

documents.title: RE: Had my surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it went smoothly. Yes, please keep the iron going every day for now. It takes months to rebuild your stores. Let's see you this summer and we'll recheck your blood count then.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Office Visit: Sleep Disturbance, Leg Discomfort
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective
Follow-up for her iron deficiency, now about 3 months on ferrous sulfate. Fibroid was resected hysteroscopically in May. Periods are shorter since then, 6 to 7 days, but still heavy.

Main concern today is sleep. For about three months, once she lies down at night she gets an overpowering need to move her legs, with a deep buzzing feeling inside both calves. Moving or walking makes it go away, but it comes right back once she is still again. She is up several times a night pacing the hall and drags through the next day. Nothing like it during the day. Her mother has the same thing.

She eats vegetarian. Doesn't drink, no drugs. She does not snore and no one has seen her stop breathing in sleep. Taking the iron daily.

Objective
Vitals per flowsheet. Neuro: strength, reflexes, sensation and gait normal. Legs: no edema, no varicosities or skin changes of venous disease. Pulses normal.

Assessment
1. Restless legs syndrome — meets criteria. Iron deficiency likely contributes.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, on oral iron; ongoing menstrual losses plus a vegetarian diet.
3. Submucosal fibroid, resected; marking resolved.

Plan
- Ropinirole 0.5 mg at bedtime, start tonight; discussed sleepiness and nausea; avoid driving if drowsy.
- Continue ferrous sulfate daily. Ferritin and CBC today; for restless legs the goal is to get ferritin well up.
- Requesting the operative report from gyn.
- Phone check in 3 to 4 weeks.

documents.title: Ferritin and blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin is up to 10.8 from 9.2 in April — good progress. Ferritin (iron stores) is 21, better than 8 but still low, and low iron can make restless legs worse. Keep taking the iron every day with juice. We'll recheck in the fall.

documents.title: Ropinirole check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt for follow-up per PCP. Taking ropinirole nightly at 9 pm. Says she is getting up once a night at most now and usually sleeps through. No daytime sleepiness. Continue current dose. Message routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second request to the gynecology office for the 5/20 operative note and pathology. First fax 7/13 not answered. Spoke with their records clerk; will fax this week.

reports.text: Specimen: uterine mass, hysteroscopic resection. Gross: a 3.0 cm tan-white whorled fragment of rubbery tissue with an attached stalk. Microscopic: interlacing fascicles of bland smooth muscle cells without atypia, necrosis or increased mitotic activity.

procedures.procedure: Hysteroscopic excision of leiomyoma of uterus

documents.title: Operative report: hysteroscopic myomectomy
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY — OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of procedure: 05/20/2022, ambulatory surgery
Preop/postop diagnosis: submucosal leiomyoma, menorrhagia
Procedure: operative hysteroscopy with resection of submucosal myoma
Anesthesia: general (LMA)
Allergies: NKDA

Findings: a pedunculated 3 cm fibroid on a stalk from the anterior uterine wall, protruding to the internal os. Remainder of the cavity regular. Both ostia seen.

The stalk was resected at its base and the myoma removed in one piece. Hemostasis good. Fluid deficit within limits. No complications. Discharged home the same day.

Path: see report.

[Received by fax 8/30, filed. PCP reviewed.]

36-year-old here for her yearly exam; also covers the follow-up she missed in March.

Interval: energy better than last year. No more ice chewing. Periods heavy for the first couple of days, about a week total, no clots like before. Restless legs controlled on ropinirole at bedtime, maybe one restless night a week. Taking iron most days.

Allergies: none.
PMH: iron deficiency anemia; restless legs; submucosal fibroid s/p hysteroscopic resection 5/2022.
Social: unchanged; vegetarian.

ROS otherwise negative. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well. Conjunctivae pink. Nails normal now. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No leg swelling. Neuro grossly normal.

Plan:
- Iron deficiency anemia: CBC, ferritin. Keep iron.
- RLS: stable, same dose, refills sent.
- Health maintenance: CMP, lipids. Pap due next year. Fall flu and COVID.

documents.title: Office Visit: Exertional Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
37F with iron deficiency anemia (on iron) and restless legs (on ropinirole). Since roughly early February she has been getting winded with things that used to be easy: one flight of stairs, carrying groceries from the car. Tired by mid-afternoon. Worried the anemia is back, since that is how it felt in 2022, though no ice cravings this time. No cough, wheeze, fever, chest pain, palpitations or fainting. No ankle swelling. Periods unchanged. Never smoker.

Meds: ferrous sulfate 325 daily, ropinirole 0.5 qhs. NKDA.

Exam: comfortable at rest, speaking full sentences. Vitals per flowsheet. Conjunctivae pink. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated. Lungs clear to the bases. No clubbing. No leg swelling.

A/P: exertional dyspnea and fatigue, about 6 weeks, out of proportion to her usual activity. Recheck CBC and ferritin, BMP, TSH today. Of note her maternal aunt has pulmonary arterial hypertension. Referring to pulmonology for evaluation regardless of today's labs. Return sooner if she gets chest pain, fainting or swelling.

documents.title: Yesterday's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is normal and your iron stores are holding, so anemia doesn't explain the breathlessness. Thyroid and kidney tests are normal too. The pulmonology referral went in yesterday; their office should call you within a week or two. Let me know if they don't.

documents.title: Lung doctor update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the lung specialist last month. They did an xray that day and I had the heart ultrasound on Tuesday. Haven't heard results yet. Did they send you anything?

documents.title: RE: Lung doctor update
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Tamika, we haven't received notes from them yet. We've faxed a request and will let the doctor know as soon as anything arrives.

documents.title: Heart catheter test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The lung doctor wants a right heart catheterization next week (the 11th) to measure pressures. Is that something I should be nervous about?

documents.title: RE: Heart catheter test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: It's a common, generally safe test. A thin tube goes through a vein, usually in the neck or arm, into the right side of the heart to measure pressures directly. Most people go home the same day. It will give the specialists a clear answer. Happy to talk by phone if you want.

documents.title: New diagnosis
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I saw pulmonology again last Wednesday. They told me I have pulmonary arterial hypertension, the same thing my aunt has. They started me on tadalafil, 2 pills every morning. I'm a little overwhelmed. Can I still take my iron and leg pill with it?

documents.title: RE: New diagnosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm sorry, that is a lot to take in. Yes, iron and ropinirole are fine alongside tadalafil. We still don't have their notes, so I'm asking them again for the letter and test reports. Let's plan a visit in the fall to go over everything together, and message me anytime before then.

documents.title: Fill history reviewed
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy fill history pulled after pt's message: tadalafil 20 mg tabs, #60, filled 7/5/24, prescriber an outside pulmonologist, 2 tabs daily. Also ferrous sulfate and ropinirole, filled on schedule. Not added to our med list until we have the specialist's note; PCP aware.

documents.title: Records request: pulmonology
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called the pulmonology group; our May and July faxes were not on file there. Re-faxed signed release. Asked for consult notes from April and July plus the chest x-ray, echo and catheterization reports.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. The central pulmonary arteries are prominent. Lungs are clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size within normal limits. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Prominent pulmonary arteries. No acute cardiopulmonary process.

reports.text: Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size with preserved systolic function and normal wall motion. Right ventricle dilated with reduced systolic function. Aortic and mitral valves structurally normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function. Normal left ventricular size and function.

reports.text: Right heart catheterization via the right internal jugular vein under local anesthesia. Mean pulmonary artery pressure 45 mm Hg. Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure 10 mm Hg. Cardiac output reduced. No complications; sheath removed with hemostasis.
reports.conclusion: Precapillary pulmonary hypertension: mean PA pressure 45 mm Hg with wedge 10 mm Hg and reduced cardiac output.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY ASSOCIATES — FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 07/03/2024
Copy to: primary care

Ms. Kenney, 37, returns after her workup. Since about February she has had steadily worsening breathlessness and fatigue. She now has to stop before she finishes a block, and sometimes feels lightheaded when she pushes herself. She denies chest pain and leg swelling.

History: iron deficiency anemia on oral iron; restless legs on ropinirole; submucosal fibroid, resected 2022. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol. Family: maternal aunt with PAH.

Vitals: within normal limits today.
Exam: lungs clear. JVP elevated. Right-sided S3. P2 loud.

Data: CXR 4/23 with prominent pulmonary arteries. TTE 5/14 shows a dilated, hypokinetic RV with a normal LV. RHC 6/11: mPAP 45, PCWP 10, cardiac output reduced.

Impression: pulmonary arterial hypertension, precapillary hemodynamics.

Plan: start tadalafil 40 mg once daily (two 20 mg tablets). Reviewed headache, flushing and the absolute rule against nitrates. Return in 6 months, sooner if worse.

— Pulmonology attending

Enclosed: CXR, echo and catheterization reports.
[Received 9/10 after third request. PCP reviewed; PAH added to problem list. Discuss meds at fall visit.]

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily

1. Pulmonary arterial hypertension — managed by pulmonology, on tadalafil. Reminded no nitrates; tell any ER or dentist she takes it.
2. Iron deficiency anemia — CBC and ferritin today.
3. RLS — stable.
4. Prevention — flu, updated COVID, and PCV20 given today given chronic heart-lung disease.
Physical in January with Pap.

documents.title: Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Ms. Kenney, 39, for her yearly wellness visit. Ongoing care for PAH (pulmonology), iron deficiency anemia, restless legs; fibroid resected 2022. All of these were worked up here and by specialists between 2022 and 2024.

Today she says she is tired all the time, has been for months. She has slipped out of the exercise she used to do and hasn't really been active at all for more than a year. Sits at a desk all day. She misses being in shape. When I raised a routine, she agreed it would probably help, but isn't sure she has the time or the energy for it right now. Asked what an easy starting point would look like; did not want to commit to anything specific today.

Pulmonology saw her in August; she says it was routine and the tadalafil dose did not change (no letter received from that visit). Iron: still missing doses some weeks. Periods heavy a few days each month. RLS controlled on ropinirole.

Meds: tadalafil 40 mg daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; ropinirole 0.5 mg qhs. NKDA.
Social: administrative assistant. Never smoker. No alcohol.
PHQ-2: 1.

Exam: tired-appearing but in no distress. Vitals per flowsheet; weight up a little from last year. Conjunctivae pink. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No leg swelling. Neuro nonfocal.

Assessment and plan:
1. Fatigue, with low activity, in someone with PAH and iron deficiency. CBC, ferritin, CMP, TSH today.
2. Physical activity — she is thinking about it but not ready. Gave her a few low-effort starting ideas (a short walk at lunch, stretching at her desk) and suggested she ask pulmonology how hard she can safely push. Will revisit.
3. PAH — per pulmonology, continue tadalafil.
4. Iron deficiency anemia — continue iron; results to follow.
5. RLS — stable, refill.
6. Prevention: flu and COVID done in October; Pap current to 2030; mammography starts at 40, next fall.
Follow-up in about 6 months.
